title: [finding] `packages.ts:337` promises a wire-field rename that the objectui follow-up measured out — the comment is now a false pointer
body:
Observation-class finding, filed unassigned by the spec-surface PM seat (#6298, session `session_016R9de1FqP7NvwKvqXi92Gh`) while closing #6955. For triage to grade.

## The fact

`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:337` (framework `origin/main`) keeps the `publish-drafts` response's diagnostic field names `unhiddenApps` / `unhideError` deliberately, with the comment promising: *"The rename rides the objectui follow-up card, together."*

That follow-up card was #6955, and its dev measured the rename **out** rather than in (OS-DEV-REPORT on #6955, 2026-08-11): the server still emits the old names (`packages.ts:419`, `:426`; the `metadata:reloaded` announce reads `unhiddenApps` at `:444`), and objectui reads **neither field anywhere** (zero grep hits repo-wide). Under the card's own "rename in lockstep, or not at all" rule, the resolution was *not at all* — PM-ratified as option A on #6955: a rename of a zero-reader diagnostic payload buys no capability (startup-scope discipline).

## What is wrong now

Nothing at runtime. The defect is the comment itself: it promises a rename to a card that has closed without performing it, so the next reader of `packages.ts:337` is pointed at work that was measured out and will never arrive — the same false-pointer class as #7441 (a source comment contradicting a made decision).

## The fix shape (one comment edit)

Reword `:337` to record the settled state: the old spellings are kept deliberately and permanently; the planned lockstep rename was resolved "not at all" on #6955 (zero consumers on either side of the wire); cite #6955 and, if the triage grade wants it, the option-B escape hatch (a producer-side rename card) for the day someone independently wants the vocabulary tidy.

## Dedup

Searched open issues for `unhiddenApps` / `unhideError` — the only history is #6955's own thread and the #6942 framework half; no open card owns the comment. #6955 is closed by objectui#4238's merge (in convergence at filing time).

Refs: #6955 (the measurement + ruling), PR #6942 (where the promise was written), objectui#4238 (the follow-up that resolved it).
